How Commento and Heptaplus relate: shared exegetical method, extraction of formulations, Genesis-first vs myth-first

notes: Every Commento claim is Allen's report of it (essay is the only route; Garin 1942 and Jayne 1984 are cited in endnotes only). Note page markers in the middle of quotations force '...' in the gate. Crux 1: Allen says Pico identifies second hypostasis with Angel/Angelic Mind and cites Proclus, Hermias, Syrianus and the Areopagite (l. 6083-6085), but also that Pico was not yet well acquainted with Hermias's Phaedrus commentary (l. 5858-5861); Allen does not reconcile them. Crux 2: l. 6488-6492 says an Empedoclean discord vision seems foreign to Pico, yet l. 6199-6208 reports Commento 2.8 defining beauty as friendly enmity and citing Empedocles; and l. 6496-6500 says Pico wants a fourth world for man while l. 6607 says man is not even a fourth world but the bond of three. Crux 3: Allen's only explicit statement of a Commento-Heptaplus link is l. 5797-5798 (extracted formulations) and l. 6535-6540 (both engage an authoritative text); l. 6390-6393 says Genesis looms for Pico much more than for Ficino. Crux 4: Jayne (via Allen l. 6788) calls a Commento 2.13 sentence a mistake. OCR: 'dualisdc' (dualistic), 'land of exposition' (kind), 'tided' (titled), 'subsequendy'; note numerals run into text; the notes to l. 6720 block use Garin (edition pages) then Jayne's translation in square brackets. Lead check: Metatron appears only as Enoch's transformation (l. 6000-6001) and Pico's spelling 'Matatron' (note 23); no discussion of Metatron as the Agent Intellect. No claim about the Ficino Parmenides commentary beyond one endnote. Ungrounded warnings: none at last run.
